paragraphs.text: translated by
1. HERBS that sprang up in time of old, three ages earlier than the Gods,-
paragraphs.original: या ओषधीः पूर्वा जाता देवेभ्यस्त्रियुगं पुरा ।
paragraphs.translit: yā oṣadhīḥ pūrvā jātā devebhyastriyugaṃ purā |

paragraphs.text: Of these, whose hue is brown, will I declare the hundred powers and seven.
paragraphs.original: मनै नु बभ्रूणामहं शतं धामानि सप्त च
paragraphs.translit: manai nu babhrūṇāmahaṃ śataṃ dhāmāni sapta ca

paragraphs.text: 2. Ye, Mothers, have a hundred homes, yea, and a thousand are your growths.
paragraphs.original: शतं वो अम्ब धामानि सहस्रमुत वो रुहः ।
paragraphs.translit: śataṃ vo amba dhāmāni sahasramuta vo ruhaḥ |

paragraphs.text: Do ye who have a thousand powers free this my patient from disease.
paragraphs.original: अधा शतक्रत्वो यूयमिमं मे अगदं कृत
paragraphs.translit: adhā śatakratvo yūyamimaṃ me agadaṃ kṛta

paragraphs.text: 3. Be glad and joyful in the Plants, both blossoming and bearing fruit,
Plants that will lead us to success like mares who conquer in the race.
4. Plants, by this name I speak to you, Mothers, to you the Goddesses:
Steed, cow, and garment may I win, win back thy very self, O man.
paragraphs.original: सनेयमश्वं गां वास आत्मानं तव पूरुष
paragraphs.translit: saneyamaśvaṃ gāṃ vāsa ātmānaṃ tava pūruṣa

paragraphs.text: 5. The Holy Fig tree is your home, your mansion is the Parna tree:
paragraphs.original: अश्वत्थे वो निषदनं पर्णे वो वसतिष्कृता ।
paragraphs.translit: aśvatthe vo niṣadanaṃ parṇe vo vasatiṣkṛtā |

paragraphs.text: Winners of cattle shall ye be if ye regain for me this man.
6. He who hath store of Herbs at hand like Kings amid a crowd of men,-
Physician/Vaidya is that Bipra/sage's name, fiend-slayer, chaser of disease.
7. Herbs rich in Soma, rich in steeds, in nourishments, in strengthening power,-
All these have I provided here, that this man may be whole again.
8. The healing virtues of the Plants stream forth like cattle from the stall,-
Plants that shall win me store of wealth, and save thy vital breath, O man.
9. Reliever is your mother's name, and hence Restorers are ye called.
paragraphs.original: इष्कृतिर्नाम वो माताथो यूयं स्थ निष्कृतीः ।
paragraphs.translit: iṣkṛtirnāma vo mātātho yūyaṃ stha niṣkṛtīḥ |

paragraphs.text: Rivers are ye with wings that fly: keep far whatever brings disease.
10. Over all fences have they passed, as steals a thief into the fold.
paragraphs.original: अति विश्वाः परिष्ठा स्तेन इव व्रजमक्रमुः ।
paragraphs.translit: ati viśvāḥ pariṣṭhā stena iva vrajamakramuḥ |

paragraphs.text: The Plants have driven from the frame whatever malady was there.
11. When, bringing back the vanished strength, I hold these herbs within my hand,
The spirit of disease departs ere he can seize upon the life.
paragraphs.original: आत्मा यक्ष्मस्य नश्यति पुरा जीवगृभो यथा
paragraphs.translit: ātmā yakṣmasya naśyati purā jīvagṛbho yathā

paragraphs.text: 12. He through whose frame, O Plants, ye creep member by member, joint by joint,-
From him ye drive away disease like some strong arbiter of strife.
paragraphs.original: ततो यक्ष्मं वि बाधध्व उग्रो मध्यमशीरिव
paragraphs.translit: tato yakṣmaṃ vi bādhadhva ugro madhyamaśīriva

paragraphs.text: 13. Fly, Spirit of Disease, begone, with the blue jay and kingfisher.
paragraphs.original: साकं यक्ष्म प्र पत चाषेण किकिदीविना ।
paragraphs.translit: sākaṃ yakṣma pra pata cāṣeṇa kikidīvinā |

paragraphs.text: Fly with the wind's impetuous speed, vanish together with the storm.
paragraphs.original: साकं वातस्य ध्राज्या साकं नश्य निहाकया
paragraphs.translit: sākaṃ vātasya dhrājyā sākaṃ naśya nihākayā

paragraphs.text: 14. Help every one the other, lend assistance each of you to each,
All of you be accordant, give furtherance to this speech of mine.
paragraphs.original: ताः सर्वाः संविदाना इदं मे प्रावता वचः
paragraphs.translit: tāḥ sarvāḥ saṃvidānā idaṃ me prāvatā vacaḥ

paragraphs.text: 15. Let fruitful Plants, and fruitless, those that blossom, and the blossomless,
paragraphs.original: याः फलिनीर्या अफला अपुष्पा याश्च पुष्पिणीः ।
paragraphs.translit: yāḥ phalinīryā aphalā apuṣpā yāśca puṣpiṇīḥ |

paragraphs.text: Urged onward by Brhaspati, release us from our pain and grief;
16. Release me from the curse's plague and woe that comes from Varuna;
Free me from Yama's fetter, from sin and offence against the Gods.
17. What time, descending from the sky, the Plants flew earthward, thus they spake:
No evil shall befall the man whom while he liveth we pervade,
paragraphs.original: यं जीवमश्नवामहै न स रिष्याति पूरुषः
paragraphs.translit: yaṃ jīvamaśnavāmahai na sa riṣyāti pūruṣaḥ

paragraphs.text: 18. Of all the many Plants whose King is, Soma, Plants of hundred forms,
Thou art the Plant most excellent, prompt to the wish, sweet to the heart.
19. O all ye various Herbs whose King is Soma, that o'erspread the earth,
Urged onward by Brhaspati, combine your virtue in this Plant.
20. Unharmed be he who digs you up, unharmed the man for whom I dig:
paragraphs.original: मा वो रिषत्खनिता यस्मै चाहं खनामि वः ।
paragraphs.translit: mā vo riṣatkhanitā yasmai cāhaṃ khanāmi vaḥ |

paragraphs.text: And let no malady attack biped or quadruped of ours.
21. All Plants that hear this speech, and those that have departed far away,
Come all assembled and confer your healing power upon this Herb.
paragraphs.original: सर्वाः संगत्य वीरुधोऽस्यै सं दत्त वीर्यम्
paragraphs.translit: sarvāḥ saṃgatya vīrudho'syai saṃ datta vīryam

paragraphs.text: 22. With Soma as their Sovran Lord the Plants hold colloquy and say:
paragraphs.original: ओषधयः सं वदन्ते सोमेन सह राज्ञा ।
paragraphs.translit: oṣadhayaḥ saṃ vadante somena saha rājñā |

paragraphs.text: O King, we save from death the man whose cure a Brahman undertakes.
23. Most excellent of all art thou, O Plant thy vassals are the trees.
paragraphs.original: (तु. ब्रह्मपुराणम् [[ब्रह्मपुराणम्/अध्यायः १२०|२.५०.१४]]) त्वमुत्तमास्योषधे तव वृक्षा उपस्तयः । उपस्तिरस्तु सोऽस्माकं यो अस्माँ अभिदासति
paragraphs.translit: (tu. brahmapurāṇam [[brahmapurāṇam/adhyāyaḥ 120|2.50.14]]) tvamuttamāsyoṣadhe tava vṛkṣā upastayaḥ | upastirastu so'smākaṃ yo asmām̐ abhidāsati

paragraphs.text: Let him be subject to our power, the man who seeks to injure us.
